title: Atomic optimizer commit + replay endpoints for safe rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and ship a set of control-plane endpoints and SDK helpers that enable atomic, idempotent commits for Optimize recommendations (batching/caching profiles), safe roll-forward and rollback, and reliable webhook delivery/replay. This ticket covers: 1) an atomic commit API that accepts a signed transaction bundle (recommendations + target scopes + preconditions) and returns a stable transaction id; 2) server-side deduplication via idempotency tokens and semantic hashing so retries are safe; 3) a transparent rollforward/rollback protocol with explicit 'dry-run', 'apply', 'confirm' and 'revert' phases; 4) webhook delivery with ack semantics and a replayable dead-letter queue for failed webhooks; 5) SDK primitives for generating idempotency keys, building signed bundles, and reconciling local state after partial failures. Goal is to make programmatic Optimize automation safe for production customers and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments where network partitions and eventual consistency are more common.
acceptance_criteria: Commit endpoint accepts a transaction bundle with precondition checks and returns 200 + transaction_id on first submit
Repeated submits with same idempotency token return the original transaction_id and do not create a duplicate change
SDK exposes helpers to create idempotency tokens and to sign transaction bundles (HMAC using KMS key reference)
API supports dry-run mode that validates plan, estimates cost delta, but does not change live config
Rollback endpoint reverts a applied transaction within configured retention window and emits audit log entries
Webhook delivery implements at-least-once semantics with acknowledgements and moves irrecoverable failures to a replayable DLQ
End-to-end integration tests for commit -> webhook ack -> confirm and for network failure replay scenarios
Docs and console UX surfaces transaction status and per-transaction cost delta
implementation_notes: API: POST /v1/optimize/transactions -> validate bundle, compute semantic hash, allocate transaction_id, persist transaction record (states: pending/dry-run/applied/confirmed/reverted)
Idempotency: accept client-provided token and server compute stable hash; store mapping token -> transaction_id with TTL; use HMAC-signed token to prevent replay across accounts
Preconditions: support optional 'expected_config_version' and quick checks against current config; reject if precondition fails with structured error
Rollback: POST /v1/optimize/transactions/{id}/revert -> create compensating transaction; mark original as reverted and link audit entries
Webhook: reliable delivery with exponential backoff, per-webhook ack (HTTP 2xx) semantics; maintain delivery_history and attempt_count; push failures to DLQ after N attempts
DLQ replay API: POST /v1/optimize/webhooks/{id}/replay -> allows authenticated retry with visibility into last error and headers
SDK: Go/TypeScript helpers to generate idempotency keys, sign bundles, and poll transaction status (with jittered backoff)
Compatibility: design must work in Private deployments where the control plane may be behind a VPN; fall back to polling-based webhook replacement if push is unavailable
testing_plan: Unit tests for semantic hash and idempotency token verification
Integration test: submit bundle twice concurrently from different clients -> expect one transaction recorded and both clients receive same transaction_id
Chaos test: simulate control plane DB partition and ensure client retries and eventual de-dup succeed
Webhook failure tests: 500 responses -> ensure exponential backoff and DLQ entry; DLQ replay manually verified
End-to-end staging run using a canary account: dry-run -> apply -> confirm -> revert
Security test: ensure SDK bundle signing rejects modified payloads and HMAC verification fails for tampered tokens
rollout_plan: Feature-flag API behind 'optimize.transactions.v1' toggle; default off for existing customers
Internal dogfood: enable for two non-critical customer accounts and ramp after 48h of clean telemetry
Expose dry-run to all customers before enabling apply by default
Gradual enablement for Dedicated customers with migration guide for on-prem webhook endpoints
Monitor for duplicate-apply anomalies and temporarily pause rollout if duplicates > 0.1% of transactions
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: transactions.duplicate_retries_count (should be near zero after fix)
Dashboard: per-account transactions with latency histogram and cost_delta distribution
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after design workshop with Product and SRE. Key trade-off: server-side TTL for idempotency mapping vs permanent mapping for audit. Prefer TTL + audit log.
2025-02-12 - Luca Moreno: Spike complete. Verified semantic hash collision risk is negligible for our payload shapes; using sha256(hmac_key, canonicalized_bundle) as primary dedupe key.
2025-02-14 - Priya Kaur (PM): UX request: transaction view should surface expected cost delta, risk score, and links to affected routes in Console. Adding as acceptance criteria.
2025-02-16 - Security review (brief): recommend KMS HMAC signing and bounded replay window for DLQ replay to reduce attack surface. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-02-17 - Luca Moreno: Initial API stub merged to feature branch. Integration tests queued; SDK helper prototypes in PRs linked above.
